summary: No holding's thesis broke on news today. The account lost $2.46 (about -0.4%) while the SPY benchmark fell about 1.9%. Most of the loss came from the US core ETFs (VOO -1.89%, VTI -1.81%) on Nvidia, rates and crypto-led risk-off headlines. SPY closed at 739.95, 1.46% above the 729.31 200-day reference, so the VOO and VTI stops are NEAR. EXEL fell 2.75% to $67.10, 3.2% above its $65 stop, and is the nearest single-name stop. The rest of the book was flat to slightly up and had only supportive or routine company news: BNP raised WMT's target to $144, Evercore raised KR's to $75, Goldman raised MSCI's to $748, and DPZ launched a new product after Baird's 11-13 upgrade. No 4.01, 4.02 or large 1.01/2.01 filing appeared on any holding. The one unresolved filing is WMT's 8-K 5.02/9.01, filed 11-16 with a document dated 11-13, three sessions before the confirmed 11-19 print. Its content isn't in my inputs and no headline explains it, so I can't say whether a senior executive left.
upcoming:
Held names, checked for every holding against its own file estimate and filings (L2):
- WMT reports 11-19, company-confirmed. It is high risk because it is three trading days out (11-17, 11-18, 11-19). The 11-16 8-K 5.02 is unread. If the morning inputs show it is a senior executive departure, the PM's 11-16 note says the Proposer should bring a WMT reduction. The run of target raises keeps building (BNP $144, after Wells Fargo $135, BofA $139, UBS $149 and others), so the bar for the print is crowded and high. Target, Home Depot, TJX and Lowe's also report this week and are the read-across. A close-based $119 stop does not protect against a gap on the print.
- Nvidia reports 11-17. The date is from earlier runs' Benzinga 'Nov. 17 earnings' items; Nvidia isn't in today's events file. It is the first print under an interim CEO, after Huang's resignation and now Treasury Secretary Bessent pressing Nvidia over China chips. Analysts cut NVDA targets again today (Benzinga 11-16 roundup). This is the dated risk for VOO and VTI while SPY sits only 1.46% above its 200-day reference. My earlier QQQ and VOO high flags graded mostly wrong at 5 days, so read this as event risk, not a direction call.
- MCO, bought today: its CFO presents at the JPMorgan conference on 11-17. The 11-13 8-K 8.01/9.01 is still only inferred to be the euro notes deal. The 'Moody's missed estimates' line in the 11-13 CNBC 'Final Trades' roundup probably refers to the October Q3 print, not a new event (inference); there is no 8-K 2.02 or guidance item in the window. Moody's affirming Willis Towers Watson's ratings is routine business. Next earnings 2027-02-17.
- KR reports 12-03, company-confirmed. Its 10-17 grocery-chain cyber-incident flag is about a month old and still has no confirming headline or filing, so it is drifting toward 'came to nothing'.
- INCY's 11-13 MAESTRA-3 cancellation (8-K 8.01) said guidance is unaffected. There has been no follow-up.
- Other next dates: EXEL 2027-01-11 (file estimate), FAST 2027-01-19, MSCI 2027-01-27, IDXX 2027-02-01, VRSN 2027-02-04, MCO 2027-02-17, CARG 2027-02-18, DPZ 2027-02-22.

Sleeves:
- Rates: traders now price Fed hikes in December and January (11-14). The next hard date is the 12-09 FOMC. BND was sold today, so no bond ETF is held.
- Crypto: a fifth leg down, with BTC at about $64K on 11-16 after $69K on 11-13. ETF outflows, liquidations and Anthropic-IPO rotation are the cited causes. No exchange failure was reported. The agent holds no crypto; the shadow book does.
- GLD: Goldman told clients to wait until 2027 and trimmed its 2026 target; ETF outflows continue. This continues the 11-13 below-$4,000 break. GLD is not held.

Not held, entering the 5-day window: BLBD 11-23 estimate (8-K 5.02 from 11-10 still unread), ADSK and BBY 11-24 estimates (Telsey raised BBY's target to $110), and FTDR's unread 11-12 8-K 5.02.
